evals.name: Plain limit question
evals.prompt: What's the max number of records per record type in Workfront Planning?
evals.expected_output: Answers 25,000, notes the roadmap target of 50,000 initially rather than unlimited, and states that this cap is the same across all tiers.
assertions: States the 25,000 records-per-record-type cap
Notes the roadmap target is 50,000 initially, not unlimited
Notes this particular cap does not vary by tier
Reads references/limits-and-tiers.md rather than quoting a number from memory
Does not claim the limit is unlimited

evals.name: Customer asking for a limit exception
evals.prompt: A large enterprise customer is asking us to raise the 500 connected records limit to 2,500. They've hit it on day one of go-live. What should I tell them?
evals.expected_output: Reframes the request as an architecture problem rather than a limit problem, notes that the projected volume would exhaust even a raised cap within a couple of quarters, and offers customer-ready framing language.
assertions: Cites the 500 connected-records cap and treats hitting it on day one as a design signal
Recommends redesigning the record model before pursuing an exception
Points out that a raised cap would be exhausted again within a couple of quarters at the customer's projected volume
Notes that the 500 cap applies to multi-select non-hierarchy connections and does not change by tier
Loads references/limits-and-tiers.md and references/customer-conversation-framings.md
Does not negotiate an intermediate number such as 1,500
Does not concede that the limit is generally negotiable

evals.name: Customer asking for P95 data
evals.prompt: A customer is meeting with us tomorrow and wants P95 performance numbers for Planning. What can we share?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Adobe publishes no public P95 or SLA, and that internal numbers may only be shared framed explicitly as observed production telemetry.
assertions: States that Adobe does not publish a public P95 or SLA for Planning
Frames any internal numbers as observed production telemetry, server-side
Explicitly distinguishes telemetry from a contractual guarantee
Advises how to frame the numbers if they are shared externally
Does not present the numbers as a commitment or suggest they can go into a contract

evals.name: RPM industry comparison
evals.prompt: A customer is comparing our 200 RPM API rate limit to other SaaS APIs and saying it's low. How do I defend it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that 200 RPM per user is defensible for an interactive planning product, identifies bulk integrations sharing interactive user accounts as the real trap, and recommends separate service accounts for bulk traffic.
assertions: States the 200 RPM per-user rate limit and why it suits interactive use
Identifies bulk integrations sharing user accounts with interactive use as the actual problem
Recommends separate service accounts for bulk traffic instead of raising the limit
Does not benchmark against high-frequency data APIs, which are a different product category

evals.name: Tier-aware limit question
evals.prompt: What are the object limits for Workfront Planning, and do they differ by tier?
evals.expected_output: Explains that object limits scale by tier (Select, Prime, Ultimate) and that the tier must be established before answering a limit question.
assertions: Names the Select, Prime, and Ultimate tiers
States that object limits scale by tier
Asks for or establishes the customer's tier before giving specific numbers
Reads references/limits-and-tiers.md rather than guessing limit values

evals.name: Workspace design from scratch
evals.prompt: Help me design a Workfront Planning workspace for a global marketing team that runs campaigns across 30 countries with multiple channels and brands.
evals.expected_output: Proposes a multi-workspace design with a central taxonomy hub, separates work record types from reference record types, and avoids the known deviations of the Fréscopa exemplar.
assertions: Separates work record types (Campaigns, Tactics, Experiences) from reference types (Countries, Channels, Brands, Audiences)
Proposes a central taxonomy hub rather than duplicating shared lists across workspaces
Recommends 2 to 3 configured views per work record type
Keeps sections within the 3 to 6 per workspace range
Loads references/workspace-build-playbook.md and references/best-practice-template.md
Does not put lifecycle fields on pure reference types
Does not propose a single mega-workspace for all 30 countries
Does not reproduce the Fréscopa template wholesale

evals.name: Record type or field
evals.prompt: We have 'Priority' and 'Campaign Sponsor' as concepts in Workfront Planning. Should they be record types or fields on Campaign?
evals.expected_output: Applies the heuristic: Priority is a single-select field with fixed values and no data of its own; Campaign Sponsor depends on whether sponsors carry attributes worth tracking.
assertions: Recommends Priority as a single-select field rather than a record type
Makes Campaign Sponsor conditional on whether sponsors have attributes worth tracking
Explains the underlying heuristic rather than only giving the verdict
Does not reflexively model both concepts as record types

evals.name: Misclassified reference type
evals.prompt: In our reference template we have a 'Pillars' record type with Status, Start Date, and End Date fields. Is that right?
evals.expected_output: Flags that Pillars is likely misclassified as a reference type when it carries lifecycle attributes, and recommends either reclassifying it or removing the lifecycle fields.
assertions: Identifies that lifecycle fields on a reference type indicate misclassification
Recommends moving it to a work or activity type, or removing the lifecycle fields
Cites this as a known deviation in the Fréscopa template rather than an endorsed pattern
Does not approve the structure merely because the reference template contains it

evals.name: Specify a complete workspace build
evals.prompt: Specify a Q1 campaign workspace build for Workfront Planning. Marketing team running 4 product lines, 5 regions, and 3 audience segments.
evals.expected_output: Produces a complete build specification in the canonical order (workspace, sections, record types, fields, connections, sample records, views), presented once at the end.
assertions: Follows the build order: workspace, sections, record types, fields, connections, sample records, views
Specifies each record type fully before moving to the next
Includes 2 to 3 views per work record type
Refers to objects by display name rather than raw IDs
Presents the finished design once instead of narrating each intermediate step
Does not stop after specifying only the workspace shell

evals.name: CASE function availability
evals.prompt: Is the CASE function supported in Workfront Planning formula fields?
evals.expected_output: Answers yes, notes that the public documentation omits CASE, and treats observed API behavior as canonical over the public formula docs.
assertions: Confirms CASE is supported
Notes that public documentation omits it
Treats observed API behavior as canonical over the public formula docs
Does not conclude the function is unsupported merely because the public docs omit it

evals.name: Formula authoring and unsupported functions
evals.prompt: My Workfront Planning formula field keeps failing. I'm trying to use SWITCH to map status values. Also, write me a formula for budget variance percentage between Total Budget and Actual Spend.
evals.expected_output: Identifies SWITCH as unsupported, suggests CASE instead, and produces a variance formula using curly-brace field references with exact display names, noting decimal storage.
assertions: States that SWITCH is not supported in Planning formulas
Suggests CASE as the supported alternative
Wraps field display names in curly braces with exact case and spacing
Produces a correct variance expression against Total Budget
Notes that percentage values are stored as decimals, where 0.15 represents 15 percent

evals.name: Compound API filter
evals.prompt: How do I search for active Workfront Planning campaigns in EMEA launched after Jan 1 via the API?

assertions: Uses $-prefixed operator tokens rather than UI labels
Expresses the filter as a JSON array rather than an object
Combines conditions with $and
Uses ISO 8601 dates with a mandatory Z timezone
Uses $hasAnyOf for the Region reference field rather than a text operator
